Regional Regulation of Central Lombok Regency number 3 of 2009 concerning Protection of children and women victims of violence has been in force for approximately 14 years. During the period of its validity, there have been many changes in policies and laws and regulations in the field of Protection of children and women, whether adopted by the central government, provincial government or Central Lombok regency government. Therefore, at the regency regional regulation level, adjustments need to be made so that the Central Lombok regency government has a legal basis for implementing policies and programs in the field of Protection of women and children.

The field of regional government has undergone changes with the revocation of Law Number 32 of 2004 concerning Regional Government by Law Number 23 of 2014 concerning Regional Government. Based on article 12 of Law Number 23 of 2014 concerning Regional Government, the affairs of women's empowerment and child protection constitute Mandatory Government Affairs that are not related to Basic Services. In the appendix to Law Number 23 of 2014 concerning Regional Government, the division of regency government affairs in the field of women's empowerment and child protection is regulated in more detail. The field of women includes the following authorities: a). Prevention of violence against women involving parties within the scope of the regency/city Region. b). Provision of services for women victims of violence requiring coordination at the regency/city Region level. c. Strengthening and development of institutions providing Protection services for women at the regency/city Region level. Field. Quality of Life of Women includes, Institutionalization of gender mainstreaming at regional government institutions at the regency/city Region level. b. Empowerment of women in the political, legal, social and economic fields in community organizations at the regency/city Region level. c. Strengthening and development of institutions providing women's empowerment services at the regency/city Region level. Field of Fulfillment of Children's Rights (PHA), includes: Institutionalization of PHA in government, non-government institutions, and the business world at the regency/city Region level, Strengthening and development of service provider institutions for improving the quality of children's lives at the regency/city Region level. Field of Protection of children in special circumstances includes, a. Prevention of violence against children involving parties within the scope of the regency/city Region. b. Provision of services for children requiring special Protection that requires coordination at the regency/city Region level. c. Strengthening the development of service provider institutions for children requiring special Protection at the regency/city Region level.

Changes have also occurred in law number 23 of 2022 concerning Protection of children through two amendments, namely 1). law number 35 of 2014 concerning amendments to the law number concerning Protection of children, and 2. Stipulation of Government Regulation in Lieu of Law Number 1 of 2016 Concerning the Second Amendment to Law Number 23 of 2002 Concerning Protection of Children into Law. There are a number of obligations of regional governments contained in this law that must be further regulated by regional regulations. Changes to law number 23 of 2022 concerning Protection of children certainly have legal implications for child Protection legal policy in Central Lombok regency.

In the aspect of Protection of women, significant changes occurred when law number 12 of 2022 concerning the criminal act of sexual violence was promulgated. There are several provisions related to the obligations of regional governments that must be regulated in regional regulations: 1). Provisions of Article 76 paragraph (2) Provincial and regency/city Regional Governments are obliged to establish UPTD PPA that organizes Handling, Protection, and Recovery of Victims, Victims' Families, and/or Witnesses, 2). Article 79 paragraph (1) obligation of the Central Government and Regional Governments are obliged to organize Prevention of Criminal Acts of Sexual Violence quickly, in an integrated and integrated manner. 3). Article 80 paragraph (1) Regional Governments are obliged to organize education and training for law enforcement officials, government service personnel, and service personnel at Community-Based Service Provider Institutions, 4).

Regional Regulation of Central Lombok Regency number 3 of 2009 concerning Protection of children and women victims of violence has been in force for approximately 14 years. During the period of its validity, there have been many changes in policies and laws and regulations in the field of Protection of children and women, whether adopted by the central government, provincial government or Central Lombok regency government. Therefore, at the regency regional regulation level, adjustments need to be made so that the Central Lombok regency government has a legal basis for implementing policies and programs in the field of Protection of women and children.

The field of regional government has undergone changes with the revocation of Law Number 32 of 2004 concerning Regional Government by Law Number 23 of 2014 concerning Regional Government. Based on article 12 of Law Number 23 of 2014 concerning Regional Government, the affairs of women's empowerment and child protection constitute Mandatory Government Affairs that are not related to Basic Services. In the appendix to Law Number 23 of 2014 concerning Regional Government, the division of regency government affairs in the field of women's empowerment and child protection is regulated in more detail. The field of women includes the following authorities: a). Prevention of violence against women involving parties within the scope of the regency/city Region. b). Provision of services for women victims of violence requiring coordination at the regency/city Region level. c. Strengthening and development of institutions providing Protection services for women at the regency/city Region level. Field. Quality of Life of Women includes, Institutionalization of gender mainstreaming at regional government institutions at the regency/city Region level. b. Empowerment of women in the political, legal, social and economic fields in community organizations at the regency/city Region level. c. Strengthening and development of institutions providing women's empowerment services at the regency/city Region level. Field of Fulfillment of Children's Rights (PHA), includes: Institutionalization of PHA in government, non-government institutions, and the business world at the regency/city Region level, Strengthening and development of service provider institutions for improving the quality of children's lives at the regency/city Region level. Field of Protection of children in special circumstances includes, a. Prevention of violence against children involving parties within the scope of the regency/city Region. b. Provision of services for children requiring special Protection that requires coordination at the regency/city Region level. c. Strengthening the development of service provider institutions for children requiring special Protection at the regency/city Region level.

Changes have also occurred in law number 23 of 2022 concerning Protection of children through two amendments, namely 1). law number 35 of 2014 concerning amendments to the law number concerning Protection of children, and 2. Stipulation of Government Regulation in Lieu of Law Number 1 of 2016 Concerning the Second Amendment to Law Number 23 of 2002 Concerning Protection of Children into Law. There are a number of obligations of regional governments contained in this law that must be further regulated by regional regulations. Changes to law number 23 of 2022 concerning Protection of children certainly have legal implications for child Protection legal policy in Central Lombok regency.

In the aspect of Protection of women, significant changes occurred when law number 12 of 2022 concerning the criminal act of sexual violence was promulgated. There are several provisions related to the obligations of regional governments that must be regulated in regional regulations: 1). Provisions of Article 76 paragraph (2) Provincial and regency/city Regional Governments are obliged to establish UPTD PPA that organizes Handling, Protection, and Recovery of Victims, Victims' Families, and/or Witnesses, 2). Article 79 paragraph (1) obligation of the Central Government and Regional Governments are obliged to organize Prevention of Criminal Acts of Sexual Violence quickly, in an integrated and integrated manner. 3). Article 80 paragraph (1) Regional Governments are obliged to organize education and training for law enforcement officials, government service personnel, and service personnel at Community-Based Service Provider Institutions, 4).

Regional Regulation of Central Lombok Regency number 3 of 2009 concerning Protection of children and women victims of violence has been in force for approximately 14 years. During the period of its validity, there have been many changes in policies and laws and regulations in the field of Protection of children and women, whether adopted by the central government, provincial government or Central Lombok regency government. Therefore, at the regency regional regulation level, adjustments need to be made so that the Central Lombok regency government has a legal basis for implementing policies and programs in the field of Protection of women and children.

The field of regional government has undergone changes with the revocation of Law Number 32 of 2004 concerning Regional Government by Law Number 23 of 2014 concerning Regional Government. Based on article 12 of Law Number 23 of 2014 concerning Regional Government, the affairs of women's empowerment and child protection constitute Mandatory Government Affairs that are not related to Basic Services. In the appendix to Law Number 23 of 2014 concerning Regional Government, the division of regency government affairs in the field of women's empowerment and child protection is regulated in more detail. The field of women includes the following authorities: a). Prevention of violence against women involving parties within the scope of the regency/city Region. b). Provision of services for women victims of violence requiring coordination at the regency/city Region level. c. Strengthening and development of institutions providing Protection services for women at the regency/city Region level. Field. Quality of Life of Women includes, Institutionalization of gender mainstreaming at regional government institutions at the regency/city Region level. b. Empowerment of women in the political, legal, social and economic fields in community organizations at the regency/city Region level. c. Strengthening and development of institutions providing women's empowerment services at the regency/city Region level. Field of Fulfillment of Children's Rights (PHA), includes: Institutionalization of PHA in government, non-government institutions, and the business world at the regency/city Region level, Strengthening and development of service provider institutions for improving the quality of children's lives at the regency/city Region level. Field of Protection of children in special circumstances includes, a. Prevention of violence against children involving parties within the scope of the regency/city Region. b. Provision of services for children requiring special Protection that requires coordination at the regency/city Region level. c. Strengthening the development of service provider institutions for children requiring special Protection at the regency/city Region level.

Changes have also occurred in law number 23 of 2022 concerning Protection of children through two amendments, namely 1). law number 35 of 2014 concerning amendments to the law number concerning Protection of children, and 2. Stipulation of Government Regulation in Lieu of Law Number 1 of 2016 Concerning the Second Amendment to Law Number 23 of 2002 Concerning Protection of Children into Law. There are a number of obligations of regional governments contained in this law that must be further regulated by regional regulations. Changes to law number 23 of 2022 concerning Protection of children certainly have legal implications for child Protection legal policy in Central Lombok regency.

In the aspect of Protection of women, significant changes occurred when law number 12 of 2022 concerning the criminal act of sexual violence was promulgated. There are several provisions related to the obligations of regional governments that must be regulated in regional regulations: 1). Provisions of Article 76 paragraph (2) Provincial and regency/city Regional Governments are obliged to establish UPTD PPA that organizes Handling, Protection, and Recovery of Victims, Victims' Families, and/or Witnesses, 2). Article 80 paragraph (1) Regional Governments are obliged to organize education and training for law enforcement officials, government service personnel, and service personnel at Community-Based Service Provider Institutions, 4).

Regional Regulation of Central Lombok Regency number 3 of 2009 concerning Protection of children and women victims of violence has been in force for approximately 14 years. Therefore, at the regency regional regulation level, adjustments need to be made so that the Central Lombok regency government has a legal basis for implementing policies and programs in the field of Protection of women and children.

The field of regional government has undergone changes with the revocation of Law Number 32 of 2004 concerning Regional Government by Law Number 23 of 2014 concerning Regional Government. Based on article 12 of Law Number 23 of 2014 concerning Regional Government, the affairs of women's empowerment and child protection constitute Mandatory Government Affairs that are not related to Basic Services. Provision of services for children requiring special Protection that requires coordination at the regency/city Region level. c. Article 36

Community participation in the implementation of Child Protection is carried out through activities:

a. provision of advice and considerations in the implementation of Child Protection,
b. dissemination of information in the context of Child Protection, Cc. provision of funds, services, as well as facilities and infrastructure in the context of Child Protection,
d. provision of education in efforts to improve Child morals, e. prevention of child marriage, Violence, exploitation, discrimination and neglect of Children, f. reporting, emergency assistance and Protection for Children experiencing child marriage, Violence, exploitation, discrimination and neglect,
g. advocacy for handling child marriage, Violence, exploitation, discrimination and neglect of Children, h. facilitation of repatriation and/or social reintegration processes, and
i. other activities that support efforts for Protection, care, and welfare of Children.

Article 21

Fulfillment of the right to education, leisure time, culture, and recreation as referred to in Article 14 letter d, is implemented through:

a. provision of educational facilities and infrastructure, b. provision of educational human resources, Cc. implementation of child-friendly schools,
d. implementation of support for the 12 (twelve) year compulsory education program,
e. guidance on early childhood education,
f. facilitation of access to education for children who are already married, g. facilitation of access to education for children in conflict with the law,
h. provision of children's playground facilities and infrastructure, i. provision of creative and recreational facilities and infrastructure, and j. provision of sports facilities and infrastructure for Children with disabilities.
